identity.title: Observational evidence for a possible link between PAH emission and dust trap locations in protoplanetary disks

paper_type_evidence.quote: High-resolution ALMA dust continuum images are available for all targets
The majority of these images have been previously published, and we use the published images for this work.

question.value: Is the 3.3 micron PAH intensity of T Tauri and Herbig disks correlated with the warm (midplane T > 30 K) millimeter dust mass, as expected if PAHs are frozen out on pebbles and only sublimate once pebbles reach warm dust traps?

evidence.quote: are compared with ALMA dust continuum images, in order to test whether there is evidence that PAHs are frozen out on pebbles in dust traps and only sublimate under certain conditions.
A sample is constructed from 26 T Tauri and Herbig disks located within 300 pc

analysis_steps.goal: derive total dust mass at 20 K

method.value: standard optically thin millimeter dust mass equation M = F d^2 / (kappa B(T)) at T = 20 K

evidence.quote: we estimate the total dust mass using the common equation related to the total millimeter flux

key_parameters.value: kappa(1000 GHz) = 10 (units as printed: g cm^-2), kappa proportional to nu^beta with beta = 1

evidence.quote: The uncertainty on this parameter is 10%, following the flux calibration uncertainty of ALMA.

assumptions.value: dust temperature 20 K and optically thin emission

evidence.quote: for an assumed temperature of 20 K and optically thin emission (cite: Hildebrand1983)

method.value: power-law passive-disk profile (Chiang and Goldreich) for non-transition disks; individually fitted RADMC-3D SED+continuum models for transition disks (or literature profiles)

evidence.quote: The midplane temperature profile of each disk is estimated using a power-law profile assuming a passively heated disk, following (cite: Chiang1997)
their temperature profiles are estimated individually using a RADMC-3D model fitting the Spectral Energy Distribution

key_parameters.value: RADMC-3D: outer radius 150 au, inner dust disk of 1 au depleted by delta_dust, scale height h(r)=h_c (r/r_c)^psi with psi = 0.15 and r_c = 50 au

evidence.quote: The vertical scale height is described by $h(r)=h_c({r}/{r_c})^{\psi}$ with $\psi=0.15$ and characteristic radius $r_c$=50 au.

assumptions.value: gas-to-dust ratio 100; small (0.005-1 um) and large (0.005-1000 um) grain populations

evidence.quote: The outer radius is set at 150 au and the surface density is scaled to the total gas disk mass $M_{\rm disk}$ with a gas-to-dust ratio of 100.
The dust opacities are computed using a combination of a small grain and large grain population, of 0.005-1 $\mu$m and 0.005-1000 $\mu$m, respectively.

fitting.value: free parameters M_disk, h_c, r_cav, delta_dust fitted to radial continuum profiles and SEDs; optimiser, priors and likelihood not stated

evidence.quote: The models were fit to both the radial continuum profiles and the SEDs.

analysis_steps.goal: compute warm dust mass inside the 30 K radius

method.value: integrate the millimeter flux from 0 to the radius where midplane T drops below 30 K, then convert to mass with the dust mass equation at T = 30 K

evidence.quote: The warm dust mass flux is computed for each disk by integrating the millimeter flux from 0 out to the radius where the midplane temperature drops below 30 K
for T=30 K, we compute the warm dust mass

evidence.quote: with the 22-30 K regime and spatial resolution indicated

assumptions.value: 30 K is a reasonable single temperature because the dust mass is dominated by the temperature at the outer radius

evidence.quote: the dust mass will be dominated by the temperature at the outer radius due to the shape of the temperature profile and 30 K is a reasonable choice

validation.value: cutoff-temperature sensitivity check: impact of changing the cutoff within 22-30 K judged generally negligible

evidence.quote: Whereas the exact cutoff temperature will impact the warm dust mass, this range shows that the impact is generally negligible.

method.value: integrate Kurucz stellar spectrum plus 10,000 K blackbody scaled to accretion luminosity over 912-2050 A; chi from L_FUV at 150 au scaled to ISRF; also at R_in and R_size

evidence.quote: The definition of the cutoff temperature of the warm dust region is thus chosen at 30 K in the midplane.

referee_caveats_inferred: Correlation is driven by upper limits and a few strong detections; 3.3 micron PAH sample is small (26) and heterogeneous (ISO, VLT, different apertures)
Warm dust mass depends on the assumed temperature law (phi = 0.02 power law) and on the 30 K cutoff; no uncertainty propagated beyond a flat 10%
Stellar luminosity and spectral type correlate with PAH excitation and with disk mass, so a confounding variable is possible
Heterogeneous ALMA images (different resolutions, wavelengths, published reductions) feed one quantity; no uniform reprocessing
Pearson r from linmix with censored data is not standard; no significance or bootstrap test of the correlation is given

products_in_archive.value: 5 targets use archive product fits files; others use published images

evidence.quote: For 5 targets we use the product fits files directly from the ALMA archive as these are sufficient for our purposes.

reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: Small to moderate: published continuum images or product fits for 26 disks, roughly a few GB if archive products are downloaded
reproducibility.score_reason: Scale 1-5. Equations, constants (kappa, 30 K cutoff, phi = 0.02) and statistics tool are given and inputs are public continuum images; weak points are unspecified radial profile geometry, linmix setup and SED model details.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Data are archival or published images, the recipe is a short calculation chain, and the headline results (Pearson r, warm dust masses) are numeric; transition-disk temperature profiles need re-derivation.
